item.title: O'Connor ranching legacy began in 1834; 6,409 acres of Texas prairie protected 191 years later
item.description: The historic T.M. O'Connor Ranch in Texas has gained a notable conservation easement, protecting nearly 6,409 acres of precious coastal prairie while enabling ranching operations to persist. Made feasible through a combination of federal and private funding under the RESTORE program, this area plays a pivotal role in supporting over 300 distinct wildlife species and rare flora. This agreement showcases a united front for conservation efforts alongside sustainable farming solutions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Boy, 6, wrote ‘Chocolate Bar’ for friend with rare liver disorder; book raised $1 million
item.description: At 6, Los Angeles boy Dylan Siegel wrote and sold a book calledChocolate Barto help fund research into his best friend Jonah’s rare liver disorder. What began as a child’s idea grew into a fundraising effort that had raised $1 million by 2014.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Iowa family’s 84-year farming legacy ends as 1,209 acres go up for auction
item.description: On October 30, a landmark auction will take place for the 1,209-acre farmland portfolio owned by the Woods family in Fayette County. This well-preserved parcel boasts high-quality soil, attracting a variety of potential buyers—from local farmers to investors and recreational users. The hybrid auction setup will enable competitive bidding on individual lots, marking the culmination of the family’s 84-year legacy with the land.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sally Quinn and Ben Bradlee bought Grey Gardens for $220,000; it later sold for $15.5M
item.description: In a momentous deal for historic preservation, Sally Quinn and Ben Bradlee acquired the storied Grey Gardens estate in 1979 for $220,000. Following a meticulous restoration, it emerged as a cultural hallmark tied to the Beales. Its remarkable sale for $15.5 million in December 2017 underscores the lasting interest in uniquely significant properties, concluding nearly forty years of history for this iconic location.

item.title: Four North Carolina homes repaired after Helene face demolition after FEMA buyouts
item.description: In the aftermath of Hurricane Helene, four homes in the Cottages at Cypress Run neighborhood in Hendersonville face demolition due to severe flooding. Previously, these homes were repaired through homeowner efforts and community volunteerism. To address the persistent flood threats, homeowners have chosen FEMA's voluntary buyouts, aligning with the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program's initiative to convert affected land into green spaces, thereby reducing future flood risks.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Queensland dairy farmer opened four campsites after drought forced her family to sell 40 cows
item.description: Agritourism is gaining momentum among Australian farmers struggling with drought-related financial pressures. Landowners like Libby Rough are transforming their properties into camping havens, creating alternative income streams. This shift not only aids in sustaining their farms during tough times but also promotes local agricultural education among visitors. Moreover, local authorities are streamlining regulations to encourage this thriving sector, enhancing community engagement with farming practices.

item.title: Georgia begins 10-year forest restoration at 132-acre Towaliga Preserve with data-centre partnership
item.description: The Towaliga Preserve is about to launch an ambitious 10-year forest restoration project, backed by QTS Data Centres. This significant initiative aims to revitalize 132 acres, focusing on ecosystem management and biodiversity enhancement. Throughout the decade, contractors will engage in tasks like invasive species control and planting native trees. After the project, the Southern Conservation Trust will ensure the area remains cared for and healthy.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 'No deadline for Sheikh Hasina's return', says Indian high commissioner in Bangladesh
item.description: High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi addressed the extradition request for Sheikh Hasina from Bangladesh, stating that the matter is under legal review, preventing a set timeline for her repatriation. He clarified that India had no involvement in her arrival, citing the dire circumstances in Bangladesh. As relations between India and Bangladesh grow increasingly strained, the new Bangladeshi government remains resolute in pursuing Hasina's extradition.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Wisconsin diver finds 17-foot canoe underwater, radiocarbon dating puts it at 1,000 years
item.description: A fascinating discovery was made by diver Mark Schachtner: an ancient dugout canoe dating back about 1,000 years in Pewaukee Lake. In partnership with Native Nations, the Wisconsin Historical Society is carefully documenting this important archaeological treasure. Researchers have assessed its condition and theorized its submersion history. This find not only contributes to Wisconsin's storied history of ancient canoes but also sheds light on Indigenous practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan commits $89 million to restore polluted Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers by 2040
item.description: Michigan's Reclaim the Rivers initiative is set to invest $89 million to tackle pollution in the Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers. This funding is dedicated to sediment removal, restoring habitats, and increasing public access for recreation. State officials envision a significant transformation by 2040, working to reverse years of industrial damage and improve water quality and ecological health across communities and the Great Lakes.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Adopted man discovers Grammy winner Michael McDonald is his biological father
item.description: A St. Louis man adopted as a baby nearly 60 years ago discovered that Grammy-winning musician Michael McDonald was his biological father after a previously unknown half-brother took a 23andMe DNA test. The discovery led to meetings with both his birth mother and McDonald, followed by a family reunion that also introduced McDonald to his grandchildren.
